interpretation: transport_pass describes API/SSE completion or acknowledged terminal/storage delivery; it does not mean an answer is correct.
semantic_pass checks only consistency of the reported box presence with this reviewed positive clip. It does not validate every motion/time claim in an answer.

The model-generated 3.75 second timestamp is not a sampling receipt. Both direct and inline inputs logged 4 planned/4 decoded endpoint frames ending 7.5 seconds; selected pixel tensors were not captured.
The identical-question controls with 4 or 8 frames streaming controls do not support an SSE-only explanation for the false empty-scene answers.
The EVS OFF comparison used the original three broad prompts. Exact any-frame/JSON EVS ON-vs-OFF controls are pending; these records do not establish or rule out an EVS-specific accuracy regression.
VIA_EVS_TOKEN_BUDGET=1 is the documented per-clip generation trigger, not evidence of a one-token visual retention cap.
Convolution checks qualify the tested native linear projection math/dispatch, not cuDNN fallback convolution or model answer quality.

Plain any-frame positive controls returned YES at 4 and 20 requested frames, while JSON positive controls returned NO at the matching 4 and 20 frame counts. The output instructions and json_object request setting change together; the format flag alone is not isolated.

Post-short-clip-fix JPEG returns HTTP 200 with a nonempty two-token NO in 1.256 s. The empty-completion software regression is resolved for this input, but the model verdict remains incorrect. The original empty-response receipt is retained.

Archive fixed-frame sampling is honored. A single-variable removal of the overly small total-video pixel override changed this positive binary verdict from rejected to confirmed; the empty control stayed rejected. The predicted 64×128 cap shrink is CPU source-derived, not a runtime pixel capture. This does not fix or qualify JSON answers.

After finite-image terminal metadata fix 12b7e2224, the actual rebuilt engine still answered No for the visible-box JPEG in 1.238 s. The 20-frame positive YES (2.482 s) and empty NO (2.555 s) controls matched their labels; all three responses were nonempty HTTP 200 stop completions and their owned EVS sessions closed. This is a remaining single-image semantic limitation, not an unresolved empty-response or terminal-metadata bug.

finite_image_terminal_metadata.contract: A finite single JPEG/PNG or semicolon image-list request emits exactly one chunk and then end-of-input. It now marks that chunk both is_first and is_last, matching the final-video-chunk contract.
finite_image_terminal_metadata.evs_handoff: One image is padded to the two-frame temporal factor; the recording-handler regression confirms terminal=True survives that padding. Short nonterminal live clips retain terminal=False.

cpu_checks.environment: Actual 3.3 CPU-only tool image; no vLLM engine/model inference. Splitter ran without unrelated service conftest; EVS used recording handler.

archive_media_fidelity.qualification: Two known archived fixtures pass typed terminal+ES delivery and box-presence consistency using an explicit opt-in binary preset with server media size defaults. Global verifier behavior and JSON controls remain unchanged; no RTSP, long-video or general semantic accuracy qualification.
